title: Understanding ABS vs. PVC in Residential Drainage
description: Selecting the right material for DWV (Drain, Waste, Vent) systems requires understanding the operational differences between ABS and PVC piping. ABS is a black, rigid plastic known for high impact resistance at cold temperatures, joined using a single-step solvent cement without primer. PVC is typically white or gray, offers high chemical resistance, and requires a two-step solvent welding process using primer followed by cement. Never mix ABS and PVC pipes directly with solvent cement unless permitted by local codes using approved transition fittings. Always check local regulations prior to selection.

PVC is typically white or gray, offers high chemical resistance, and requires a two-step solvent welding process using primer followed by cement. Never mix ABS and PVC pipes directly with solvent cement unless permitted by local codes using approved transition fittings. Always check local regulations prior to selection.
